profile.a: The five-person Global Consulting Project team.
BlackRock's Global Real Estate Research team, which supports investment teams across regions and asset classes.
How AI changes real estate demand, where it adds value in the investment process, and how BlackRock should adopt it safely.
Spring 2025, with expert interviews from 20 March to 14 April 2025; a roadmap over 0-1, 2-5 and 5+ years.
Global, with cases from the US (Redfin, URG), Australia (CoreLogic), Norway (NBIM), Canada and Singapore (CPP Investments, GIC).
AI is framed as the fourth wave of real estate change, and black-box outputs threaten the trust BlackRock needs from its clients.
Six expert interviews, case studies, a sector matrix of winners and losers, a structured AI judgement process with verification, a GenAI risk matrix and a three-horizon roadmap.

charts.title: AI's effect on demand by asset class (the deck's classification)
charts.takeaway: AI pulls demand towards the infrastructure it runs on (data centres, logistics, labs) and away from space it replaces (office and retail). For a portfolio, the implication is to tilt towards the top and reposition the bottom.

charts.title: What office occupiers value most (rating out of 10)
charts.takeaway: After location, what a building offers counts almost as much, which supports the deck's case that landlords must act as service providers. ESG certification ranks last.

charts.title: Gains reported in the AI cases (%)
charts.takeaway: The operational gains are large, but they come from vendors' own reports or targets rather than independent results, and the deck does not test them.

charts.title: The structured AI judgement process, using the data-centre demo

items.title: Ask the in-house model
items.text: 'What is the best exit for this data centre?' The answer comes back as structured data.

items.title: Expose the assumptions
items.text: REIT listing, electricity prices rising at most 5% a year, utilisation at least 80%, enough REIT liquidity, expected IRR 15%.

items.title: Verify each assumption
items.text: AI-augmented quantitative models test each one against real and synthetic data: stress tests, back-tests, causal checks.

items.title: Loop back if weak
items.text: Confidence below 60% or a failed stress test sends the result back to the model to revise.

items.title: Report
items.text: A structured, visual validation report that a client can price.

charts.takeaway: The deck's central idea: explainability means 'priceability', an answer whose assumptions a client can see, test and pay for.

charts.takeaway: Foundations first: data before models, pilots before platforms. Two expert cautions sit awkwardly with it: custom models date quickly, and generic chatbots conflict with the explainability goal.
